text:
marie: Quick RFC follow-up — proposal to run an inventory-guided slice pruning pass next quarter. Short summary: create an ownership + coupling catalog, rank candidate slices by cost & coupling, and schedule pragmatic cutovers with canaries and fallback shims. Looking for objections or additions.
jamal: +1. My ask: scope to hotpaths first (runtime & request-router). Those give the best cost/latency wins.
andre: Agree. Minimal deliverable: CSV inventory with columns -> service, owner, api_endpoints, shared_state, reqs_s, p95_ms, num_callers. That plus a coupling score.
lucy: We have partial telemetry but caller mapping is hit-or-miss. Suggest a 2-week sampled tracing window with a small tag we can use to mark "slice-candidate" traffic for easier correlation.
infra-bot: NOTE: applying a new trace tag across prod increases ingest. Recommend sampling at 1-5% and only for selected services to limit cost.
marie: Good point. Updated proposal: run sampled traces + static call-graph extraction (repo-level) and merge heuristics. Output = ranked candidate list by estimated unit-cost impact and coupling risk.
jamal: For cutovers, require a fallback shim that can re-route to the old service for 4 weeks post-cutover. That will reduce blast radius for downstream teams.
andre: Canary plan sketch: 0% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over several days. Automated rollback triggers: error rate delta > 0.5% absolute OR p95 latency increase > 15% relative. Also add golden-key test traffic hitting core inference flows.
lucy: Owners will need runbooks. I'll author two templates: "stateless handler extract" and "stateful store extract" (include migration checklist, data backfill steps, and monitoring queries).
marie: Action items (assign):
  - lucy -> runbook templates
  - andre -> inventory CSV schema + coupling scoring notes
  - jamal -> canary automation spike + rollback playbook
  - marie -> schedule 2-week sampled tracing starting Mon (will post exact start ts)
Any objections? If not, I'll kick this off EOW.
jamal: Timeline sounds good. Small add: include regression eval prompts for core inference paths (use Redwood Optimize eval harness) to detect quality drift when switching models or quantized variants.
andre: +1. Also flag any services with external contract customers or dedicated/private deployments — legal + sales need heads-up if we change APIs.
lucy: I'll add a "customer_impact" column and a "deploy_mode" tag (hosted/dedicated/private) to the inventory. Also adding a quick script to auto-detect callers via IAM role bindings as a heuristic.
marie: Nice. If no objections by EOW we'll spin up sampling. Plan to publish the initial inventory format in #eng-ops and link to this thread. :party_parrot:

Example CSV header we're going to use for the inventory (draft):
```
service,owner,api_endpoints,shared_state,reqs_s,p95_ms,num_callers,coupling_score,customer_impact,deploy_mode
```

marie: pinging @andre @lucy @jamal — please confirm you own items above, or reassign before EOD.
